head: Pakistan joined its Indus river dolphin sanctuaries into one 400-kilometre protected corridor.
summary: The Punjnad Indus River Dolphin Sanctuary, created in June 2026, protects nearly 200 kilometres of river in Punjab and connects with existing reserves in Sindh. A 2025 study estimated 1,987 dolphins, up from 617 in 2001, with 99 percent living in a 690-kilometre stretch between the Chashma and Sukkur barrages. Gillnets caused 52 percent of documented deaths from 2008 to 2023, and they remain the main threat the new protections must address.
